chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

'Whoever injures a game animal with a weapon and invokes the name of God, Mighty and Majestic, over it, then it remains for a night or two nights without a predator eating from it, and he knows that his weapon is what killed it, then he may eat from it if he so desires.'

And he said regarding a mountain goat that a man hunted, then the people tore it apart while the man was pursuing it: 'Do you consider this to be plunder?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not plunder, and there is no objection to it.'

key_terms.إِيَّل: mountain goat or stag; a type of large game animal
key_terms.بَأْس: harm, objection, or problem — 'لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْس' is a legal formula meaning 'there is no objection'
key_terms.ذَكَرَ اسْمَ اللَّه: invoking the name of God; the tasmiyya (Bismillah) required before hunting
key_terms.سَبُع: predator; wild beast that might consume the prey
key_terms.سِلَاح: weapon; in the context of hunting, this refers to any instrument that pierces
key_terms.نُهْبَة: plunder; unlawfully seized property — the Imam ruled it is not plunder in this case

ai.seo_question: Is game meat permissible if the hunted animal dies after one or two days from the weapon wound according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) provides two rulings on hunting: first, that game killed by one's weapon with proper invocation of God's name is permissible to eat even if it died after a day or two, provided no predator had consumed it; second, that a mountain goat hunted by a man but then seized and divided by others is not considered unlawful plunder, and consuming it is permissible. These rulings reflect the Shia jurisprudential approach to game laws, clarifying conditions under which hunted meat remains halal.
